analytics_report: Q1 2017 User Telemetry - Binge Watching & Scrubbing Behavior

scrubbing_behavior.error_rate: 34% of scrubs overshoot the intro and land in the episode content, causing the user to rewind

binge_watching_impact.definition: Watching 3+ episodes in a single session
binge_watching_impact.drop_off_point: Users are 4x more likely to end a session during an opening credits sequence than during the middle of an episode
binge_watching_impact.intro_fatigue_index: For users watching 4+ episodes, the probability of manual scrubbing increases from 8% on Episode 2 to 31% on Episode 4

ab_test_prototype_results.feature_adoption: 84% of users who were shown the 'Skip Intro' button clicked it within 3 seconds of it appearing
ab_test_prototype_results.time_saved: Average of 68 seconds saved per click
ab_test_prototype_results.session_length_increase: Test cohort exhibited a 6.2% increase in average binge session length (minutes watched per session)
ab_test_prototype_results.abandonment_reduction: Session abandonment during opening credits dropped to near zero (0.4%) in the test cohort

conclusion: The data overwhelmingly supports that the opening credits sequence is a primary friction point for binge-watching continuity. Introducing a one-click bypass mechanism eliminates scrubbing errors and measurably increases total session length.
